gloss: see, behold, gaze; see in vision; (a second root) breast
summary: To see and to look at, often with attention or delight: to gaze on Zion, on the beauty of Yahweh, on his face; and above all to see what Yahweh shows, so that the prophet's book is “the vision which he saw” and the prophet is a חֹזֶה “seer”. Its nouns are the vision itself (חָזוֹן, חִזָּיוֹן, מַחֲזֶה) and the false vision of prophets who “see out of their own heart”. Scripture's Aramaic uses the same verb and noun for the dreams and night visions of Daniel. The same spelling also gives חָזֶה “breast”, the priests' portion of the peace offering; its cognates (Aramaic and Syriac ḥadyā) show an older ḏ behind the ז, where those of “see” show z, so it is a second, older root in the same letters.

words.gloss: see, behold, gaze on; look out, select; see in vision
words.summary: About fifty times, nearly all in poetry and the prophets, in the qal only; the everyday verb of seeing is רָאָה, with which it stands in parallel (Isa 30:10; 33:17; Pro 24:32; Job 19:27). חָזָה is seeing that dwells on its object, and the word for what a prophet is shown. The brief's tokens with no stem (Exo 29:27 and the like) are the noun חָזֶה “breast” and the participle חֹזֶה, filed here by spelling.

stems.gloss: see, behold, gaze; perceive; look out, select; see in vision

senses.definition: To look at something and take it in: to gaze on a person or a city, to look on a man's work or a field and learn from it, to see the sun or vengeance; often in parallel with רָאָה.

evidence.note: “The king in his beauty תֶּחֱזֶינָה your eyes; they will see (תִּרְאֶינָה) a land of distances”: parallel with רָאָה.
“חֲזֵה Zion, the city of our appointed feasts; your eyes will see (תִרְאֶינָה) Jerusalem.”
Over the sluggard's field: “וָאֶחֱזֶה I, I set my heart; I saw (רָאִיתִי), I received instruction.”
“Return, return, that we may look (וְנֶחֱזֶה) on you. What will you look at in the Shulammite?”
The nations say of Zion, “let our eye gaze (וְתַחַז) on Zion”: the gloating look.
“Do you see a man skilled in his work? He will stand before kings.”
“Do you see a man hasty in his words?”
“Come, behold (חֲזוּ) the works of Yahweh.”
Like a stillborn child that has not “seen the sun”.
“The righteous will rejoice when he sees vengeance.”
“Every man has looked on it; man beholds it (יַבִּיט) from afar.”
“What I have seen I will recount”: seen, and so known.
“You yourselves have all seen it.”
“He works on the left, and I do not behold him (אָחַז); he turns to the right, and I do not see (אֶרְאֶה)”: the short form, in parallel with רָאָה.
Of a plant's roots among stones, “he looks on a house of stones”: obscure.
“You loved their bed; you looked on a hand (יָד)”: obscure, of idolatry.
“You have heard; see (חֲזֵה) all of it.”

senses.definition: To see and understand what is shown, as Yahweh's lifted hand, which the wicked will not see until they are put to shame.

evidence.note: “Yahweh, your hand is lifted up, בַּל־יֶחֱזָיוּן; יֶחֱזוּ and be ashamed”: they will not see it, but they shall see it.
“Why do those who know him not see his days?”
“What I do not see, teach me.”

senses.gloss: behold God, his face or beauty
senses.definition: To look upon God himself, his face, his beauty in his house, his power and glory in the sanctuary; the hope of the upright, and in Job the hope of the one who dies.

evidence.note: “Yahweh is righteous … the upright shall behold his face.”
“I, in righteousness, will behold your face; I will be satisfied, when I awake, with your likeness.”
“From my flesh I shall behold God, whom I shall behold for myself, and my eyes shall see (רָאוּ), and not another.”
“To behold the beauty of Yahweh and to inquire in his temple.”
“So in the sanctuary I have beheld you, to see (לִרְאוֹת) your power and your glory.”
The elders of Israel “beheld God, and ate and drank”.

senses.definition: Of Yahweh's eyes: to look on men and try them, and to see what is right.

evidence.note: “His eyes behold, his eyelids test (יִבְחֲנוּ) the sons of man”: seeing that examines.
“Let my judgment go out from before you; let your eyes behold uprightness.”

senses.definition: To look over a people and pick out men fit for a task.

evidence.note: Jethro: “you shall look out (תֶחֱזֶה) from all the people able men, who fear God … and set them over them.”

senses.gloss: see in vision, see as a prophet
senses.definition: To see what Yahweh shows a prophet, whether a sight or a word; the books of the prophets are “the vision which he saw” or “the word which he saw”.

evidence.note: “The vision (חֲזוֹן) of Isaiah son of Amoz, which he saw (חָזָה) concerning Judah and Jerusalem.”
“The word that Isaiah son of Amoz saw”: a word is seen.
Balaam: “who hears the words of God, who sees the vision (מַחֲזֵה) of the Almighty, falling down, with eyes uncovered.”
“The burden of Babylon which Isaiah son of Amoz saw.”
“The words of Amos … which he saw concerning Israel.”
“The word of Yahweh which came to Micah … which he saw concerning Samaria and Jerusalem.”
“The burden which Habakkuk the prophet saw.”
The people “say to the seers (רֹאִים), Do not see (תִרְאוּ), and to the visionaries (חֹזִים), Do not see (תֶחֱזוּ) for us right things; speak to us smooth things, see deceits.”
“The vision that he sees is for many days.”

senses.definition: Of false prophets and diviners: to “see” emptiness and a lie, visions Yahweh did not give.

evidence.note: “They have seen emptiness and lying divination, who say, Yahweh says, but Yahweh has not sent them.”
“Have you not seen a vision (מַחֲזֵה) of emptiness?”
“You shall no more see emptiness nor divine divination.”
“While they see emptiness for you, while they divine a lie for you.”
“Your prophets have seen for you emptiness and whitewash, and have not uncovered your iniquity.”
“The diviners have seen a lie and speak dreams of emptiness.”

evidence.locator: Ezk.12.27; Job.15.17; Ezk.13.7, חָזָה → ὁράω (×3); εἶδον, under εἴδω, ×15, e.g. Psa.11.7; Isa.1.1; Amo.1.1

evidence.note: “Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see (ὄψονται) God”: the hope of Psa 11:7 and 17:15.
“They shall see his face.”
“When he appears we shall be like him, for we shall see him as he is.”

parallels.note: The common verb of seeing, set beside חָזָה in parallel.
To divine: the false prophet's “seeing” is set beside divination.

phrases.gloss: which he saw: the title of a prophet's book

words.gloss: see, look; see a dream or vision; (passive participle) seemly
words.summary: Scripture's Aramaic verb of seeing, in Daniel and once in Ezra: the ordinary word for seeing in that language, used both of plain sight and of the dreams and night visions in Daniel. The brief's two qal tokens and one haphel are the same peal forms mis-filed (Isa 33:20; 48:6 are Hebrew; Dan 2:31 is the peal participle).

stems.gloss: see, look; see in a dream or vision

senses.definition: To see with the eyes: men unharmed in the fire, a hand writing on the wall; the idols that do not see.

evidence.note: “Behold, I see four men loose, walking in the midst of the fire.”
The satraps “saw these men, that the fire had no power over their bodies.”
“The king saw the part of the hand that wrote.”
“Gods of silver and gold … which do not see (חָזַיִן) and do not hear and do not know”: seeing, hearing and knowing, the marks of the living God.
Idols “which can neither see nor hear nor walk”: the same words.
“It is not fitting for us to see the king's dishonour.”
“You see that the word is gone from me.”

senses.definition: To see what God shows in a dream or in the visions of the night, above all in the formula “I was seeing (חָזֵה הֲוֵית) … and behold”.

evidence.note: “You, O king, were seeing, and behold, a great image.”
“You were seeing until a stone was cut out without hands.”
“Since you saw that a stone was cut out of the mountain without hands … the great God has made known to the king what will be after this.”
“The dream which I have seen, and its interpretation.”
“I saw a dream, and it made me afraid.”
“Daniel saw a dream and visions of his head upon his bed.”
“I was seeing until thrones were set, and the Ancient of Days sat.”
“I was seeing in the visions of the night, and behold, with the clouds of heaven one like a son of man was coming.”
Jesus to the high priest: “you will see the Son of man … coming on the clouds of heaven”, from Dan 7:13.
“I was seeing, and that horn made war with the saints.”

senses.definition: The passive participle in one verse: what was “seen” to be done, so the measure that was fitting or usual.

evidence.note: “To heat the furnace seven times more than חֲזֵה to heat it”: than was seen, the usual or fitting measure.
“Tell the vision (ὅραμα) to no one until the Son of man is raised from the dead.”

words.summary: Thirty-five times, never of ordinary sight: what Yahweh shows a prophet, a whole prophecy (the title of Isaiah, Obadiah, Nahum), and the false vision of the prophets who speak “the vision of their own heart”. A vision has its own time and will come to pass (Hab 2:3; Dan 8:17; 10:14).

senses.definition: What Yahweh shows or speaks to a prophet; where there is none, Yahweh is silent. The word is set beside the word of Yahweh, the law and counsel as what Israel lives by.

evidence.note: “The word of Yahweh was rare in those days; there was no vision breaking out.”
“Where there is no vision the people are let loose; but he who keeps the law, happy is he.”
“They will seek a vision from the prophet, but the law will perish from the priest and counsel from the elders.”
“It shall be night for you, without vision.”
“Her prophets find no vision from Yahweh.”
“I spoke to the prophets, and I multiplied vision.”
“Then you spoke in vision to your faithful one”: the promise to David.
Nathan spoke to David “according to all this vision”.
“Daniel had understanding in all visions and dreams.”
Seventy weeks “to seal up vision and prophet”.
“Like a dream, a vision of the night.”

senses.definition: A vision speaks of what is to come and has its set time; it will not fail though it tarries.

evidence.note: “Write the vision … for the vision is yet for the appointed time; it hastens to the end and will not lie; if it tarries, wait for it, for it will surely come.”
Hab 2:3 applied to Christ's coming: “he who is coming will come and will not delay.”
The proverb “the days are prolonged and every vision fails” is answered: “the days are near, and the word of every vision.”
“The vision is for the time of the end.”
“Shut up the vision, for it is for many days.”
“What will befall your people in the latter days, for the vision is yet for days.”
Men of violence “lift themselves up to establish the vision, but they shall stumble”.

senses.gloss: vision, as the title of a prophecy
senses.definition: A prophet's whole message, written as a book.

evidence.note: “The vision of Isaiah son of Amoz.”
“The vision of Obadiah.”
“The book of the vision of Nahum.”
Hezekiah's deeds “written in the vision of Isaiah”.

senses.definition: A vision claimed in Yahweh's name that he did not give: the prophets' own heart.

evidence.note: “They speak a vision of their own heart, not from the mouth of Yahweh.”
“I did not send them … they prophesy to you a false vision and divination.”
Prophets “who see a vision of peace for her, and there is no peace”.
“There shall be no more any vision of emptiness.”

evidence.locator: 1Sa.3.1; Isa.1.1; Hab.2.3; Oba.1.1, חָזוֹן → ὅρασις (×23 with ὅρασιν, ὁράσεως); Jol.3.1, חֶזְיֹנוֹת → ὁράσεις

evidence.note: Peter quotes Joel 3:1: “your young men shall see visions (ὁράσεις).”

parallels.note: The vision of the prophet beside the law of the priest.

words.summary: The qal participle as a title: one who sees what Yahweh shows, beside נָבִיא “prophet” and רֹאֶה “seer”. Gad is “David's seer”, and Heman, Asaph, Jeduthun, Iddo and Jehu son of Hanani are called by it; the books of Chronicles cite their writings. In Isa 28:15 the same word is set in parallel with בְּרִית “covenant”; how “seer” or “seeing” gives “agreement” is not yet understood.

senses.definition: A prophet as one who is shown what Yahweh will do; Yahweh warned Israel “by every prophet and every seer”. Also, of the astrologers of Babylon, one who looks to the stars to foretell.

evidence.note: “The word of Yahweh came to Gad the prophet, David's seer.”
“Yahweh warned Israel and Judah by every prophet and every seer.”
“He has shut your eyes, the prophets, and covered your heads, the seers.”
“To the seers (חֹזִים), Do not see for us right things.”
Amaziah to Amos: “Seer, go, flee to the land of Judah.”
“The seers shall be ashamed and the diviners confounded, for there is no answer from God.”
“Heman the king's seer in the words of God.”
“Samuel the seer (רֹאֶה) … Nathan the prophet … Gad the seer (חֹזֶה).”
Jehu son of Hanani the seer rebukes Jehoshaphat.
“The words of David and of Asaph the seer.”
“Jeduthun the king's seer.”
“The words of the seers who spoke to him in the name of Yahweh”; v. 19 חוֹזָי, read as “the seers”.
“The prophets who see emptiness (הַחֹזִים שָׁוְא).”
Babylon's “dividers of the heavens, who look at the stars (הַחֹזִים בַּכּוֹכָבִים), who make known by the months”: the astrologer, as Arabic ḥāzin.

senses.definition: In one verse, a pact made with the grave, in parallel with a covenant with death. The link to seeing is not clear.

evidence.note: “We have cut a covenant (בְרִית) with death, and with the grave we have made a חֹזֶה.”

evidence.locator: 2Ch.19.2; 29.30; 35.15, חֹזֶה → προφήτης; elsewhere the participle of ὁράω, e.g. 2Ki.17.13; 1Ch.21.9

evidence.note: “Many prophets and righteous men desired to see what you see.”

words.summary: Only in the law of the peace offering: the breast of the animal, raised before Yahweh and given with the right thigh to Aaron and his sons as their portion. Its cognates, Aramaic and Syriac ḥadyā “breast”, show ḏ behind the ז where the verb's show z: a different older root in the same letters, not “the seeing part”.

senses.definition: The breast of a ram or other peace offering, raised (תְּנוּפָה) before Yahweh and then eaten by the priests in a clean place.

evidence.note: “The fat with the breast he shall bring, the breast to raise it as a raised offering before Yahweh … the breast shall be Aaron's and his sons'.”
“The breast of the raised offering and the thigh of the contribution I have taken … and given them to Aaron the priest and his sons as a portion for ever.”
At the consecration Moses raises the breast of the ram, and it is his portion.
“They put the fat on the breasts … and the breasts and the right thigh Aaron raised.”
Eaten “in a clean place, you and your sons and your daughters”.
The Nazirite's offering, “with the breast of the raised offering”.
The firstborn's flesh is the priest's, “as the breast of the raised offering”.

senses.definition: In Daniel's Aramaic, the visions of the head upon the bed and of the night, in which God reveals what is to come.

evidence.note: “The secret was revealed to Daniel in a vision of the night.”
“There is a God in heaven who reveals secrets … your dream and the visions of your head on your bed are these.”
“I was seeing in the visions of the night.”
“The visions of my head troubled me.”

senses.definition: How a thing looks to the eye.

evidence.note: The little horn, “whose appearance was greater than its fellows”.

senses.gloss: a vision, visions of the night
senses.definition: A single vision, and in the plural visions; often of the night, beside dreams, and the vision Yahweh promised to pour out on all flesh.

evidence.note: “According to all these words and all this vision Nathan spoke to David.”
“In a dream, in a vision of the night, when deep sleep falls on men … then he opens the ears of men.”
“You terrify me with dreams and visions.”
“He shall fly away like a dream … chased away like a vision of the night.”
“I will pour out my spirit on all flesh … your young men shall see visions.”
Peter quotes it at Pentecost.
In that day the prophets “shall be ashamed each of his vision”.
“The burden of the valley of vision”: Jerusalem.

senses.definition: A vision shown to a prophet.

evidence.note: “A hard vision has been declared to me.”
“The vision of all this has become to you like the words of a sealed book.”

senses.definition: What is seen and stands out: the goat's horn “of sight”, a conspicuous horn.

evidence.note: “The goat had a horn of sight (קֶרֶן חָזוּת) between its eyes.”
In its place came up “four of sight”, four notable horns.

senses.definition: The pact with the grave of Isa 28:15, now annulled; in parallel with covenant. The link to seeing is not clear.

evidence.note: “Your covenant with death shall be annulled, and your חָזוּת with the grave shall not stand.”

senses.definition: A vision in which Yahweh speaks, as to Abram; or the false prophets' vision.

evidence.note: “The word of Yahweh came to Abram in a vision, saying, Do not fear, Abram.”
“Who sees the vision of the Almighty.”
“Have you not seen a vision of emptiness?”

words.summary: Only in 1Ki 7:4–5, of the windows of Solomon's house of the forest of Lebanon: as a place to look out (the Syriac noun maḥzā “sight” is the same formation). The verse sets “window against window”, so a link with the Arabic ḥāḏā “be opposite” (behind “breast”) has also been argued; the evidence does not decide it.

senses.definition: A window or light in a wall, in rows facing one another.

evidence.note: “Three rows of frames, and window against window, three times.”

senses.gloss: sight, how far a thing is seen
senses.definition: The sight of the great tree, seen to the end of the earth.

evidence.note: “Its height reached to heaven, and its sight to the end of all the earth.”

senses.definition: Once, the title of the written visions of Iddo the seer, a source of the history of Solomon.

evidence.note: “In the visions of Iddo the seer concerning Jeroboam son of Nebat.”

words.summary: Scripture's Aramaic for the breast, with ד where Hebrew has ז: the same correspondence as Aramaic דְּהַב for זָהָב, which shows the older ḏ behind Hebrew חָזֶה.

senses.definition: The chest of the image in Nebuchadnezzar's dream, of silver.

evidence.note: “Its head of fine gold, its chest (חֲדוֹהִי) and arms of silver.”

cognates.gloss: estimate by conjecture; divine, especially from birds; (ḥāzin) a diviner, an astrologer
cognates.note: Arabic keeps only the seer's side of the root: the one who looks and foretells, as the חֹזִים of Babylon who “look at the stars” (Isa 47:13). Shows ḥ behind ח and z behind ז.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 562, art. حزو and حزى, حَزْوٌ (n7914)
evidence.note: “He computed by conjecture the quantity … He divined: and particularly from the flight, or cries, &c., of birds.”

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 563, art. حزو and حزى, حَازٍ (n7916)
evidence.note: “A diviner: one who examines the members, and the moles of the face, divining … An astronomer, or astrologer.”

cognates.gloss: see, recognise, decide; (ḥezwā) looks, appearance, vision
cognates.note: Jewish Aramaic, in the Targums and Talmud: the common verb “see”, and its noun for appearance and vision, as in Daniel. Aramaic keeps z apart from ḏ (which it writes ד), so ḥzy shows z.

evidence.locator: s.v. חֲזִי (ch.), “to see, recognize, to decide”, citing Targ. O. Gen. XXIX, 10; Ber. 45a
s.v. חֶזְוָא, “looks, appearance; vision”, citing Targ. Gen. XXIX, 17

cognates.gloss: see, behold; appearance, apparition; observer, eye-witness; sight; vision, spectacle
cognates.note: The Peshitta's ordinary verb of seeing, with nouns that match the Hebrew ones: ḥezwā “appearance” (Hebrew חָזוּת, Aramaic חֵזוּ), ḥzāyā “observer” (חֹזֶה), maḥzā “sight” (מַחֲזֶה, מֶחֱזָה), ḥezwānā “vision” (חָזוֹן). Shows z, as Aramaic.

evidence.locator: root 613 KZA; lexemes 996 KZA (see; behold), 997 KZOA (appearance; aspect; apparition), 998 KZ;A (observer; spectator; eye-witness), 1001 MKZA (sight), 3531 KZONA (vision; spectacle)

cognates.note: Punic, listed in the Proto-Semitic root set *ḥzy “see” with Aramaic and Hebrew; not yet followed to an edition of the inscriptions.

evidence.locator: SEM000159 ḥzy [see] V, PUN000652 ḥzy [see] V

cognates.note: Listed in the same root set. Ugaritic d usually answers to older ḏ, which would set it against the Aramaic and Arabic z; the correspondence is irregular, so it is recorded as possible and no sound is drawn from it. Not yet checked in a Ugaritic dictionary.

evidence.locator: SEM000159 ḥzy [see] V, UGC001822 ḥdy [see] V

cognates.note: Jewish Aramaic; the Targum uses it for the breast of the ram of consecration (Exo 29:26), Hebrew חָזֶה. Aramaic ד for Hebrew ז shows an older ḏ.

evidence.locator: s.v. חַדְיָא II, “breast, chest, bosom”, citing Targ. Ex. XXIX, 26; Targ. Prov. XXIV, 33; Kidd. 70b

cognates.note: Syriac, with d for older ḏ, against ḥzā “see” with z in the same language: the two Hebrew words of this spelling come from two older roots.

cognates.gloss: be over against, opposite to, face; (ḥiḏāʾ) the front, what is opposite
cognates.note: If the breast is named as the front of the body, this is its root, with the ḏ the Aramaic and Syriac show; but the Arabic word for breast is another, so the tie is argued, not shown.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 537, art. حذو, حَاذَاهُ (n7471)
evidence.note: “He, and it, was, or became, over against, or opposite to, him, or it; faced, or fronted, him, or it.”

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 537, art. حذو, حِذَآءٌ (n7479)
evidence.note: “Also … i. q. إِزَآءٌ [The front …]”

doctrine.statement: The upright hope to “behold the face” of Yahweh (Psa 11:7). David puts the time of it: “I will behold your face in righteousness; I will be satisfied, when I awake, with your likeness” (Psa 17:15), and Daniel uses the same word of the dead: “many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake” (Dan 12:2). Job puts its manner: his redeemer lives “and at the last will stand upon the dust”, and “after my skin is struck off, yet from my flesh I shall behold God, whom I shall behold for myself, and my eyes shall see” (Job 19:25–27). Jesus promises the pure in heart that “they shall see God” (Mat 5:8); John, that “when he appears … we shall see him as he is” (1Jn 3:2); and of the city to come, “they shall see his face” (Rev 22:4). From the verses: the seeing of God is not at death but on awaking from the sleep of death, in the flesh, with one's own eyes, when Christ appears; the hope rests on resurrection, not on a soul that lives on.

Scripture sets two kinds of vision side by side. The false prophets “speak a vision of their own heart, not from the mouth of Yahweh” (Jer 23:16); “I did not send them … they prophesy to you a false vision and divination” (Jer 14:14); they “have seen emptiness … saying, Yahweh says, but Yahweh has not sent them” (Ezk 13:6), and “have not uncovered your iniquity” (Lam 2:14), but cry “peace, and there is no peace” (Ezk 13:16). The true vision has its appointed time: “the vision is yet for the appointed time … if it tarries, wait for it, for it will surely come” (Hab 2:3), which the letter to the Hebrews applies to the coming of Christ (Heb 10:37); “the days are near, and the word of every vision” (Ezk 12:23); “the vision is for the time of the end” (Dan 8:17). Where Yahweh gives no vision, his word is rare (1Sa 3:1), yet “he who keeps the law, happy is he” (Pro 29:18). From the verses: a vision is tested by its source, whether it is Yahweh's word and calls to repentance, and by its fulfilment at its time; and those to whom no new vision comes are kept by the law already given.

Nebuchadnezzar “was seeing” an image of four metals, “until a stone was cut out without hands” and struck it on its feet, and “the stone that struck the image became a great mountain and filled the whole earth” (Dan 2:34–35). Daniel interprets: “in the days of those kings the God of heaven will set up a kingdom which shall never be destroyed … it shall break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms, and it shall stand for ever”, and “since you saw that the stone was cut out of the mountain without hands … the dream is certain” (Dan 2:44–45). In his own night visions Daniel “was seeing” one like a son of man come with the clouds of heaven, to whom was given “dominion and glory and a kingdom, that all peoples … should serve him” (Dan 7:13–14), and “the kingdom … of the kingdoms under the whole heaven shall be given to the people of the saints of the Most High” (Dan 7:27). Jesus told the council, “you will see the Son of man … coming on the clouds of heaven” (Mat 26:64). From the verses: the kingdom of God is a real kingdom that takes the place of the kingdoms of men on the earth, under the whole heaven, given to Christ and to the saints at his coming.

note: Two older roots share the spelling: *ḥzy “see” (Arabic ḥazā, Aramaic and Syriac ḥzy, all z) and the root of חָזֶה “breast” (Aramaic חֲדִי, Jewish Aramaic and Syriac ḥadyā, all with d for ḏ). Open: whether מֶחֱזָה “window” (1Ki 7:4–5, “window against window”) belongs with “see” (as Syriac maḥzā “sight”) or with Arabic ḥāḏā “be opposite”; it is put with “see”. Open: חֹזֶה and חָזוּת “agreement” with the grave (Isa 28:15, 18) have no cognate or verse that explains the sense; perhaps a pact made through seers or necromancers (Isa 28:7; 29:10), not established. Ugaritic ḥdy “see” not checked in DULAT; Punic ḥzy not followed to an edition. Ge'ez ገጽ “face” is linked by Wiktionary but not followed. Dan 3:19 is filed under peal as a passive participle (could be called peil). The brief's verb h.bp.aa also counts by spelling the breast tokens (Exo 29:27; Lev 7:34; 10:14; Num 6:20) and חֹזֶה tokens; Job 23:9 אָחַז is the short qal of חָזָה. Names: Hazael, Jahaziel, Haziel, Hazaiah, Jahzeiah, Hezion, Mahazioth and Col-hozeh have name files. Left out: Hazo son of Nahor (חֲזוֹ, Gen 22:22, h.bq.ac), whose tie to the root is not shown; Gehazi (גֵּיחֲזִי, BDB c.bt.ad under גחר), whose first element is not clear; and the 0-token cross-references h.bc.ac, h.bp.ab, h.bo.ai, j.be.ah, m.bm.ak, h.bq.aa. חוֹזָי of 2Ch 33:19 is read as “the seers” (TIPNR has no person Hozai).
